description: A UniProt protein entry or a separately represented cleavage product of a polyprotein. Coverage includes manually reviewed Swiss-Prot proteins for represented organisms, including viruses, and computationally annotated TrEMBL proteins for non-virus organisms. Some organisms are represented by proteins from one representative subclass. Historical proteins can remain with obsolete set to true. Optional annotations describe ChEMBL targets and bacterial virulence factors.

common_properties.name: identifier
common_properties.description: UniProtKB identifier: UniProtKB:{primary_accession} for a regular protein, or UniProtKB:{parent_accession}-{PRO_id} for a cleavage product.

common_properties.name: name
common_properties.description: UniProt entry name for regular proteins, such as 1433B_HUMAN; a PRO identifier string for cleavage products. It is not the human-readable protein description.

common_properties.name: description
common_properties.description: Protein names from UniProt for regular entries; the specific chain annotation text for cleavage products. Regular-entry descriptions do not contain the UniProt FUNCTION free-text block.

common_properties.name: gene
common_properties.description: Gene names supplied by UniProt; ORF names, ordered locus names and gene synonyms are excluded. Cleavage products carry their parent entry’s gene names.

common_properties.name: refseq
common_properties.description: RefSeq protein and nucleotide accessions, with source formatting such as trailing periods retained. Cleavage products have an empty list.

common_properties.name: seqids
common_properties.type: list of nucleotide and protein accession strings
common_properties.description: EMBL nucleotide and protein accession fields, with raw formatting retained. Placeholder and Genomic_DNA values are excluded. Cleavage products have an empty list.

common_properties.name: org_name
common_properties.description: Source organism name, including parenthetical common names; period characters are absent.

common_properties.name: org_ncbi_id
common_properties.description: Identifier of the represented Organism. For proteins from a representative subclass, this is the parent organism rather than the protein’s original taxon.

common_properties.name: sources
common_properties.description: Contributing sources, including UniProt and, where annotated, VFDB. UniProt remains listed on historical obsolete proteins. Human ID-mapping enrichment is not separately represented in this list.

common_properties.name: last_updated
common_properties.description: Timestamp associated with creation or an update to the protein or its annotations.

source_contributions.scope: Swiss-Prot for all represented organisms and TrEMBL for non-virus organisms. Where an accession is in both, its properties reflect TrEMBL. For organisms with direct Swiss-Prot proteins, proteins from their taxonomic subclasses are excluded. Organisms without direct Swiss-Prot proteins can instead have proteins from the candidate subclass containing the longest individual protein sequence; other candidate subclasses are excluded. Cleavage products are represented when an entry has more than one qualifying CHAIN or PEPTIDE annotation: a PRO identifier, amino-acid length greater than 10, and a note not containing N-terminally. Both the parent and qualifying products, including full-span annotations, are represented.
source_contributions.description: Provides protein identity, names, gene and organism annotations, enzyme and sequence-database cross-references, and isoform information. Protein data carry the documented license annotation CC BY-NC 3.0. Human primary-accession ID mappings supplement ChEMBL cross-references; isoform-suffixed mapping rows are excluded.

properties.name: ec
properties.description: Enzyme Commission numbers, including incomplete numbers such as 3.4.24.-. This property is absent on cleavage-product nodes.

properties.name: chembl_id
properties.description: Bare ChEMBL target accession, such as CHEMBL3710403. Flat-file cross-references are supplemented by human UniProt ID mapping. Only one value is represented where several mappings exist; reviewed-protein values can be historical rather than current mappings. Cleavage products inherit the parent’s flat-file cross-reference.
properties.notes: Absent from node entirely if no ChEMBL mapping exists; never null or empty string

properties.name: isoform
properties.description: Isoform annotations including a name, FASTA header, source URL and canonical-status flag. The canonical isoform is the displayed sequence. Cleavage-product nodes lack this property.

properties.name: polyprotein
properties.description: Parent Protein identifier for a cleavage product. Absent on regular proteins.

properties.name: start
properties.description: Amino-acid start position of a cleavage product within its parent sequence.

properties.name: end
properties.description: Amino-acid end position of a cleavage product within its parent sequence.

source_contributions.scope: Bacterial proteins in VFDB that are already represented as Protein nodes, including historical obsolete proteins when listed by VFDB. One virulence factor is associated with each annotated protein.
source_contributions.description: Virulence factor identity, category, function and mechanism are properties of the associated factor and can therefore be shared by several proteins. These annotations supplement the protein’s UniProt identity and organism information.

properties.name: vf_id
properties.description: Virulence factor identifier, stored bare, for example VF0464.

properties.name: vf_name
properties.description: Short name of the protein’s virulence factor.

properties.name: vf_full_name
properties.description: Full name of the protein’s virulence factor.
properties.notes: Always present; empty string `""` when the source value is empty

properties.name: vf_category
properties.description: Functional category of the virulence factor, such as Immune modulation or Effector delivery system.

properties.name: vf_function
properties.description: Free-text description of the virulence factor’s function.
properties.notes: Always present; empty string `""` when the source value is empty

properties.name: vf_mechanism
properties.description: Free-text description of the virulence factor’s mechanism.
properties.notes: Always present; empty string `""` when the source value is empty
